7.  Formation  of Active
  City Manager Russi reported on the Formation of Active Transportation
  Transportation Committee  Committee.
  He stated that per the direction given by the City Council following
  the March 18, 2019 study session,  staff  is submitting Resolution 19- 36, to
  Council for the purpose  forming
  of  an  Active Transportation  Committee.  The
  nine- member committee' s main focus will be to ensure roadways enable safe,
  attractive, comfortable, and independent access and travel for all active
  transportation uses and motorists.

  Mayor Kendrick called for public comment.

  Pam  Berry, La Verne resident,  asked  if the City Council
  would be recruiting for
  all five residents for the board.

  Mayor Kendrick and Council Member Carder both replied that currently there
  are three residents who have been serving on a subcommittee on
  transportation for several years and they have agreed to serve on the new
  Committee. The City will be recruiting for two residents to serve on the
  Committee.

  Council Member Hepburn stated it was important to involve as many residents
  as possible.  He spoke  about  the importance  of
  transparency and how the City
  is changing.  He s#ated he would like to serve on the Active Transportation
  Committee.

  Council Member Davis stated it was important to fully engage residents and he
  nominated Council Member Carder to serve on the Active Transportation
  Committee.

  Council Member Carder  stated  she  nominates  Council  Member Davis.  She
  stated that his involvement in the Bicycle Coalition makes him a good fit and
  she also nominated Council Member Hepburn.

  It was  moved  by Davis and seconded  by Kendrick, and unanimously carried to
  approve  Resolution  No. 19- 36, along with the attached  Exhibit A, approving the
  formation of  an  Active Transportation  Committee; Approve  Resolution No.
  19- 37, approving  the amended  list of conflict  of  interest  code.  Fill the public
  positions  as  discussed in the  staff report.  Appointed Council Members Hepburn
  and  Davis to the Committee,  recruit  for two  residents,  and appoint the three
  residents  already  on  the sub- committee.

9.  Los Angeles County feasibility  Mayor Pro Tem Rosales requested the topic of the Los Angeles County
  study  feasibility study for providing fire services be brought back before the City
  Council.  This request  is consistent  with the Council' s rules of reconsideration.

  Mayor Pro Tem Rosales  stated this matter has been addressed  several times
  and he was conflicted on this matter. He knows La Verne has an excellent Fire
  Department  and  worrieslosing
  about  them.  He stated he was not against
  doing the study and would like to know what the study would provide in regard
  to the cost and service.
  He stated in interest of transpancey and to see what
  the County can provide, he moved that the City do the Fire Feasibility Study,
  seconded  by Council Member Davis, Motion stood.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, June 17, 2019, Page 6

  Council Member Carder stated that she stands firm that she did not support
  doing the study. She stated she was concerned with the County coming in with
  a low bid and later
  raising the cost.  She stated that La Verne residents want
  their own fire department.
  She stated that if the City Council does agree to
  conduct a fire service feasibility study, she would like the study to reflect
  apples to apples in exact services.

  Mayor called for public comment:

  The following La Verne residents opposed the fire study and the City of
  La Verne going County for fire services.
  They stated the County would not
  provide the same level of services especially response time as the La Verne
  Fire Department.

  Terry Prentice
  Jeff Bassler
  Gary Hunter
  Craig Walters
  Matt Svatos

  Council Member Davis stated that he was still in favor of doing the study to see
  the difference  in cost  and  services.  He stated he was pleased with the
  resident' s interaction at the meeting and he spoke about the importance of
  continuing to engage in dialogue on this important matter.

  Council Member Hepburn agreed with Mayor Pro Tem Rosales, about the
  importance of transparency.
  He stated that it was just a study to see what the
  County can provide in services and cost. He stated that ultimately, La Verne
  residents would have to make the final decision.

  Mayor Kendrick  thanked the residents  for their  great  comments.  He stated
  La Verne has a fablulous fire Department and they do a great job. He stated
  he has not heard any positive comments from La Verne residents in having
  Los Angeles County Fire Department in the City. He spoke about the
  importance of the proposed tax measure.

  It was moved by Rosales, seconded by Davis, and carried by a vote of 3- 2,
  Carder and Kendrick No) to do the fire study.

11.  Public Comment
  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items  not  listed in any other  place  on  the agenda.  Mayor Kendrick  called for
  public  comment.

  Mark Peterson, La Verne resident stated he lives behind the golf course and
  was concerned with the orange covered chain- link fence being put around the
  perimeter of the golf course and behind his home. He urged the City Council to
  be proactive to prevent the owner from destroying the property.

  City Manager reported the City Attorney sent a letter to the property owner,
  advising them of the City' s Municipal Code process in regards to fencing and
  landscape  maintenance  requirements,  if golf course is closed.

  Robin Walker La Verne resident spoke about Sierra La Verne Golf Course and
  the owner installing orange covered chain- link fence around the golf course.
  She urged the City Council to be proactive to prevent the owner from
  destroying the property.

  George May, La Verne Library Manager reported on the library events for the
  month of June, 2019.

  Anna Anderson asked about the Hillside Specific Plan standards in regards to
  Sierra La Verne Golf Course.  She spoke about the orange- covered fencing
  which takes away from the beauty of the area.

  Jeff Bassler, La Verne resident, spoke about Sierra La Verne Golf Course and
  code enforcement things the City can do.

  Gary Hunter, La Verne resident, asked what is being done regarding the
  property at Wheeler and Foothill.
